scenario: A product team gives you a free afternoon. Which problem pulls you in first?

options.label: Make a confusing screen feel obvious and polished
Untangle the rules and data flow behind a slow feature
Explore usage data to explain an unexpected pattern
Investigate how the feature could fail, break, or be misused

scenario: Which technical system would you most enjoy understanding deeply?

options.label: A real-time game world with physics and responsive controls
A mobile app that works smoothly across devices and network conditions
A cloud platform that stays available during sudden traffic spikes
A data platform that turns messy events into trustworthy datasets
Why a model is accurate for one group but weak for another
How an attacker might move through a system without being noticed
Which rare sequence of actions causes a product defect
Where memory, concurrency, or rendering time is being lost

scenario: What kind of ownership sounds most motivating?

options.label: Take one user feature from idea through interface and API
Craft the interaction quality of a web experience
Own a reliable service used by several other teams
Build an experience people carry, touch, and use every day

scenario: A request is vague. What would you naturally do first?

options.label: Map the user journey and test a small prototype
Define the data model, boundaries, and API contract
Turn the uncertainty into a measurable hypothesis and experiment
List assumptions, edge cases, and ways to verify the result

scenario: A production feature suddenly fails. Where do you want to start?

options.label: Reproduce the user flow and inspect browser or device state
Follow traces through services, queues, and databases
Read infrastructure metrics and stabilize the service first
Check access patterns, audit logs, and possible compromise

scenario: Which blank-page project would you choose?

options.label: An offline-first phone app that uses notifications and sensors
A small game with movement, rules, sound, and progression
A pipeline that cleans, validates, and serves live event data
A low-level tool that makes other programs faster or safer

scenario: Which improvement would give you the strongest sense of progress?

options.label: An interface becomes faster, accessible, and easier to understand
A service handles ten times the load with simpler code
A model evaluation becomes reproducible and meaningfully better
Automated checks prevent an entire class of regressions

scenario: When the solution is unclear, which approach feels most natural?

options.label: Build something small, show it, and refine from feedback
Clarify constraints and design stable contracts before coding
Compare alternatives with data and controlled experiments
Map risks and create checks before changing the system

scenario: Which kind of detail are you most likely to notice?

options.label: A confusing interaction, visual inconsistency, or accessibility gap
A schema assumption, missing lineage, or inconsistent record
A memory allocation, frame drop, or concurrency hazard
An untested boundary, weak permission, or incomplete failure case

scenario: Which kind of change are you most comfortable handling?

options.label: Frequent product feedback and changing feature priorities
Slow, careful evolution of foundational architecture
Live operational conditions that require fast, calm decisions
Repeated hypothesis changes as new evidence appears

scenario: Which collaboration would energize you most?

options.label: Pairing with design and product to simplify a user problem
Working with app teams to ship a complete customer feature
Helping teams share reliable platforms, services, and data
Reviewing evidence with researchers, testers, or risk specialists

scenario: Which outcome would make your work feel most meaningful?

options.label: People can complete something important with less friction
A system quietly serves millions of requests reliably
A decision becomes clearer because the evidence is trustworthy
Users and teams are protected from avoidable failures

scenario: What kind of professional growth matters most to you?

options.label: Owning complete features and understanding the whole product
Developing a distinctive craft in interaction and presentation
Becoming the person who can solve a difficult technical core problem
Setting standards that make an organization safer and more dependable

scenario: Which description of excellent work appeals to you most?

options.label: Creative, visible, and immediately useful to people
Technically deep, efficient, and built to last
Evidence-driven, explainable, and intellectually challenging
Repeatable, observable, and resistant to mistakes

scenario: Which demanding day would still feel worthwhile?

options.label: A fast release cycle with many small product decisions
A service incident where the team must restore stability calmly
Several uninterrupted hours tracing one difficult technical defect
An experiment that fails but teaches you what to try next

scenario: Which learning path would you choose for the next month?

options.label: Accessibility, interaction design, browser behavior, and visual systems
Distributed systems, APIs, databases, and service design
Statistics, experimentation, machine learning, and data quality
Operating systems, security, automation, and performance

scenario: Which portfolio artifact would you be proudest to explain in an interview?

options.label: An accessible interactive product with thoughtful user research
A well-designed service architecture with clear reliability trade-offs
A reproducible model or dashboard built from carefully validated data
A test, security, performance, or simulation tool that exposes hidden problems
